title: Preeclampsia — Severe Features / HELLP
sources: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 222: Gestational Hypertension and Preeclampsia. Obstet Gynecol. 2020;135(6):e237-e260.
Martin JN Jr, et al. The spectrum of severe preeclampsia: comparative analysis by HELLP syndrome classification. Am J Obstet Gynecol. 1999;180(6 Pt 1):1373-1384 (Mississippi Triple-Class System).

changelog.change: Initial entry — a genuine content gap. Companion to the existing preeclampsia-eclampsia-hellp reference module (which covers management); this is the bedside severe-features checklist itself, cross-linked both directions.
Reformatted for reading on a phone: long paragraphs broken into short paragraphs and lists. Wording and clinical content unchanged.

purpose: Any ONE severe-feature criterion present converts preeclampsia to 'preeclampsia with severe features' — this checklist makes that any-one-positive logic explicit rather than requiring you to hold seven criteria in your head.

options.label: SBP ≥ 160 or DBP ≥ 110 (persistent, ≥ 2 readings ≥ 4 h apart, or treated urgently)
Transaminases ≥ 2× upper limit of normal, or severe persistent RUQ/epigastric pain unresponsive to medication and not explained by an alternative diagnosis
Creatinine ≤ 1.1 mg/dL and not doubled from baseline
Creatinine > 1.1 mg/dL, or doubled from baseline, without other renal disease
New-onset, unresponsive to medication, not explained by an alternative diagnosis

interpretation.label: Preeclampsia WITHOUT severe features
interpretation.risk: Management (inpatient vs. expectant outpatient) depends on gestational age and trend — not an emergency by this checklist alone, but reassess frequently since features can develop rapidly

interpretation.label: Preeclampsia WITH severe features
interpretation.risk: Inpatient management, magnesium sulfate for seizure prophylaxis, treat severe-range BP, and involve OB/MFM for delivery-timing decisions by gestational age

notes:
Only ONE positive criterion is needed to call severe features — this is a checklist, not a point-threshold score; the total shown is really just a count of how many criteria are met.

HELLP syndrome (Hemolysis, Elevated Liver enzymes, Low Platelets) is itself a form of severe preeclampsia and automatically satisfies this checklist via the platelet and/or liver criteria.

HELLP severity is separately graded by the Mississippi Triple-Class System, based on the platelet nadir:
- Class 1 ≤ 50,000/µL (most severe)
- Class 2 50,001-100,000/µL
- Class 3 100,001-150,000/µL

All classes also require AST/ALT ≥ 40 U/L and LDH ≥ 600 U/L to meet the HELLP lab definition itself.
buildNote: Additive engine repurposed for any-one-positive logic (each criterion worth 1 point, any total ≥1 = severe features) rather than a summed severity score — matches how ASPECTS and other non-traditional additive uses are handled in this codebase. Cross-references preeclampsia-eclampsia-hellp (management reference) via aliases/keywords since calculators don't carry a `related` field.
